If you're an RTS guy, you've probably been patiently waiting for Ashes of the Singularity to drop, thanks to statements like this, which used to be on their FAQ, unchanged for over a year:

What platforms will Ashes of the Singularity be on? Windows PC for now, but we are entirely confident that weâ€™ll release Ashes on MacOS, SteamOS, and Linux. Oxide Games is part of the Khronos group, which is developing the next-gen Vulkan graphics API that should be the API of choice on those platforms. This gives us great confidence in getting Ashes and Nitrous running on those platforms in the not-too-distant future.

Well, the game released at the end of March, and with that release came a nifty website update. Notice anything missing? All talk about a Linux or Mac client, indeed Vulkan and the Khronos group entirely, has been removed.

Unfortunately, the Wayback Machine doesn't parse the Steam forums, so I can't show you an archived copy of the development roadmap, but it's no secret that the thing was edited on release day, and when confronted, they outright deny any claims to a Mac client, while placing Linux squarely in the "maybe" category. They're just as cagey about it on Facebook.

TLDR: Ashes of the Singularity probably won't release for Linux. All evidence that they ever planned such a release has been scrubbed, and they're denying Mac outright. It's pretty obvious that Oxide Games is another outfit that promises the world, then fails to deliver. This is a black mark for Stardock.
